notes: Setup: the public Connection row and each contact's identity row are inserted by the tool (stack.connection / stack.admit), as the tool's other scenarios do. Everything else goes through the signed Telegram webhook, the real router, Chat service API and Runs with the real model.

Blocked by the defect above: no file can ever become an asset, so 'contact A uploads a file, contact B reads it by path or asset id' and 'instructions embedded in an attached file' cannot be run through a real attachment. Text pasted as file content is used instead for the injection suite and is labelled as such.
Static registry introspection imports dist/tools.js; it is not a product entry point. The behavioural evidence is the model's own tool-call attempts below (Runtime journal).
The model did not attempt shell_exec when asked directly in this run, so the call-time refusal was not exercised here.

Local file/shell tools (file_list, file_search, file_read, file_write, file_patch, shell_exec) are declared to every Run, including public IM Runs, and refused only at call time ("not available on im"). They are not Studio tools.

FAKES, labelled: phase 2 runs on a second Stack whose Runtime is started with lib/moderator-stand-in-preload.mjs: (1) the content moderator that refuses every upload says 'allowed' (defect above), (2) a module-load hook lets the attachments.* tools through the model-declaration filter in dist/agentRuntime.js (otherwise the model is never offered ls/grep/read, see scenario 11). Records, object storage, text extraction, ls/grep/read, scoping, dispatch and the model are the product's own.

defects.title: A `public` Connection on the shared Telegram bot cannot take anyone: unknown senders are told to connect from Studio
defects.expected: Spec: `public` takes anyone as a contact (router.ts meets an unknown sender on a public Connection).
defects.actual: A first-time sender on a public Product Connection received "请先从 Hatch Studio 连接 Telegram。" and no identity was created: PostgresConnections.resolveConnection returns undefined for an empty scope (the shared bot's scope), so ChannelRouter never reaches connections.meet(). Public contacts only work where the platform has a tenant scope.
defects.repro: Insert a public Product Connection, post a Telegram webhook from a sender id that was never admitted; observe the 'please connect from Hatch Studio' reply and zero hatch_channel_identities rows.

defects.title: Chat attachments cannot work on the real Runtime: no content moderator is ever configured, so every upload is refused
defects.expected: Spec (Attachments): upload first, reference by assetId, ls/grep/read answer from the file. An IM contact sending a document gets it processed.
defects.actual: A document from a Telegram contact is refused with "Uploads are unavailable: no content moderator is configured on this server.". openChatAssets() in src/chat/openChatAssets.ts builds the AssetPipeline with options.moderator ?? new UnavailableModerator(), and src/index.ts never passes a moderator (Studio's openProductAssets reads aliyunModeratorFromEnvironment; Chat does not). The same refusal answers REST uploads (see scenario 11).
defects.repro: Start the Runtime with a Postgres, POST /v1/conversations/:id/assets?name=a.txt with any bytes, or send a Telegram document to an IM Connection: 503/unavailable with 'no content moderator is configured on this server'.
